records.region: Northern La Pampa, Argentina: Rancul-side inland plain toward the Realicó-side depression belts.
records.material_pending_reason: Independent readable evidence establishing the ordinary receiving-floor links across part12 and parts17–19, between the separately visible depression/lagoon settings. Those unresolved links prevent a completed name-scope hold; more precise current flow or bank alignment is not the missing requirement.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No supported representative natural-river name was established. Naming remains subordinate to the unresolved inter-depression receiving links.
records.completion_scope: The selected La Pampa route crosses wooded and cultivated inland plain, shallow depressions and lagoon belts, then ends in a cultivated tract. Local terrain and final-setting correspondence were read across all24 parts, but two substantial inter-depression receiving links remain unestablished. No representative river name is supported, so the single result is source-material pending; no name is accepted or applied.
records.supported_name_scope: No supported representative natural-river name was established. Naming remains subordinate to the unresolved inter-depression receiving links.

scope_limits: The full selected land extent was visually inspected. The primary pending state concerns the receiving links across the long upper-middle cultivated interval (part12) and southern cross-depression interval (parts17–19), rather than uninspected image coverage.
Dry, wetland, lagoon and cultivated passages can correspond at ordinary receiving-floor scale. No continuously wet channel, exact bank match or current water-management proof was required.

The available sources do not establish whether the cross-belt portions form one connected ordinary receiving floor or need transfers between separate local depression systems. No claim of a proven drainage divide or absence of natural runoff is made.
The final cultivated endpoint is not replaced by a neighboring lagoon. Source and render endpoint descriptions remain separate even though their supplied locations coincide.
No whole-route natural-river name, true alias, exact source, current hydrological state or official river length has been established. The rendered length is selection metadata.
Exact held SEGEMAR and other identified publication limits remain in force; none was acquired or used. This is not an institution-wide prohibition.

records.source_endpoint_description: The supplied source endpoint is classified endorheic and coincides with the supplied render endpoint. Its local setting is the eastern cultivated depression plain; the metadata class is not an independently verified basin designation.
records.render_endpoint_description: The rendered selection ends in the same cultivated tract. It is not extended or moved to a nearby lagoon, named waterbody or apparent outlet.

records.region: Eastern Idaho, Modoc–Beaver–Camas corridor and Mud Lake
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the researched Modoc–Beaver–Camas stream composite ending within Mud Lake. It does not rename the distinct upper Modoc and Beaver reaches, refuge waterbodies or terminal lake.
records.completion_scope: Bounded full-path correspondence and representative receiving identity complete. No further acquisition is needed for this finding.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the researched Modoc–Beaver–Camas stream composite ending within Mud Lake. It does not rename the distinct upper Modoc and Beaver reaches, refuge waterbodies or terminal lake.

scope_limits: Map/source dates differ by contributing layer; current access is not a current field survey.
Current water flow, wetness, water-control operation and exact bank or channel alignment were not established and are unnecessary for ordinary connected-corridor correspondence.
The opening is a chosen interior Modoc Creek position, not a demonstrated official source point. Paul Reservoir is not a selected crossing.
The generalized refuge route is assessed within connected stream, marsh and lake-side settings. It does not assign every selected position to one active managed thread.
No formal naming-register determination, legally exact name transition or Korean rendering was verified.
Beaver Creek and Modoc Creek are separate component names; Mud Lake and Rays Lake are waterbody names. They are not aliases of Camas Creek.

bounded_name_observations.name: Modoc Creek
bounded_name_observations.scope: Chosen opening and north/northeast/east upper receiving corridor into Beaver Creek.

bounded_name_observations.name: Beaver Creek
bounded_name_observations.scope: Main selected valley from the Modoc join past Humphrey and Dubois to the Camas receiving junction. Separate tributary name, not an alias of Camas Creek.

bounded_name_observations.name: Camas Creek
bounded_name_observations.scope: Lower receiving stream from the Beaver junction through refuge/modified-channel settings to Mud Lake.

bounded_name_observations.name: Mud Lake
bounded_name_observations.scope: Both terminal settings and final lake-interior extension. Not a river-name alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rays Lake
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named lower refuge lake-side receiving setting along the generalized selection; no exact current wet thread assigned.

bounded_name_observations.name: Paul Reservoir
bounded_name_observations.scope: Separate small reservoir southeast of the chosen opening; no selected crossing.
Mapped Beaver-valley tributary context only; no additional selected tributary fragment exists.
Refuge and terminal neighborhood features distinguished from the representative system name; no claim that the selected route traverses every listed feature.

records.region: Chupadera Mesa and northern Jornada del Muerto, Torrance and Socorro counties, New Mexico, United States
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-drainage identity for the complete researched composite. Arroyo Seco is a separately named selected upper reach; the chosen unnamed feeder and final diffuse basin-floor passage are not individually renamed. Chupadera Draw is the field-study name explicitly equated with the mapped Chupadera Arroyo.
records.completion_scope: Full ordinary geographic correspondence for all 24 parts of FID 9879, logical 3125, mainstem stage 3, including the chosen opening, named upper reach, junction, lower dry corridor and coincident source/render ending. A representative receiving-system identity is supported; formal naming and product application remain unset.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-drainage identity for the complete researched composite. Arroyo Seco is a separately named selected upper reach; the chosen unnamed feeder and final diffuse basin-floor passage are not individually renamed. Chupadera Draw is the field-study name explicitly equated with the mapped Chupadera Arroyo.

scope_limits: The representative name does not replace the unnamed opening, Arroyo Seco or the diffuse terminal-floor setting with one scalar natural-river name.
Ordinary connected corridor/floor geography is established; exact banks, present wetness, storm-flow behavior and current water-management operations are not.
Small water patches and local crossings are not an exhaustive pond or infrastructure inventory. No glacier or large through-lake passage is depicted along this selection.

Individual imagery epochs and map-source survey dates were not established. Some northern terminal-image patches are cloudy; clear independent topography supplies the affected receiving-floor context.
The Archaeology Southwest page title uses Chupadero while its body uses Chupadera. That uncorroborated title spelling is not included as an alias.
Formal registry status remains unverified; no accepted or Korean name and no application to product data is made.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rancho Viejo Arroyo

records.region: Chihuahua, Mexico: southern interior washes, the El Llano lowland and the northern closed-playa receiving corridor in the Camargo–La Cruz area.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The sources provide geographic correspondence and bounded waterbody/place labels, but no readable river name is positively attached to the complete selected composite or to a representative receiving river. Lake/depression names cannot be substituted for an unsupported river-system identity.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No single natural-river hydronym was established for the full composite of upland washes, dry receiving flats and terminal playa. The mapped El Llano waterbody/depression name and nearby separate waterbody names are not promoted to a river-system name.
records.completion_scope: All 32 stored parts are covered by the complete original photographic view, separately inspected clean southern/middle/northern enlargements and the two relevant municipal Relieve maps. The final northern part extends outside the municipal map evidence and is covered by imagery through the actual playa-interior ending. Ordinary geographic continuity across the dry alluvial receiving floors is complete. The unresolved issue is the unsupported whole-composite natural-river name, not a missing wet thread or an unexamined lake-to-feeder transfer.
records.supported_name_scope: No single natural-river hydronym was established for the full composite of upland washes, dry receiving flats and terminal playa. The mapped El Llano waterbody/depression name and nearby separate waterbody names are not promoted to a river-system name.

scope_limits: No whole-system river name, upper part-level hydronym or northern terminal-playa name was established.
El Llano, Laguna Los Tanques, Las Arenosas and El Milagro are separate bounded waterbody/setting names, not aliases of one natural river.
Continuous ordinary receiving-floor geography does not establish permanent surface flow, present lake overflow, operating water transfers or exact wet-channel alignment.
The photographic mosaic date was not verified. The municipal maps are historical generalized compilations, not current hydrological or administrative surveys.
The northern ending is covered photographically but not by either acquired municipal map. No unacquired La Cruz map or discovery-only hydrology excerpt is treated as cartographic evidence.

bounded_name_observations.name: El Llano
bounded_name_observations.scope: The Camargo Relieve map places this waterbody label in the central receiving depression traversed by the selected lowland corridor. This is a bounded geographic name, not a name for all the selected river parts. The municipality’s hydrography table classifies El Llano as intermittent.

bounded_name_observations.name: Laguna Los Tanques
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named adjacent to the southeastern approach to the El Llano lowland in the Camargo map. The label is retained as local setting only; no exact selected shoreline crossing or alias relationship with El Llano is asserted.

bounded_name_observations.name: Las Arenosas
bounded_name_observations.feature_type: separate mapped waterbody and eastern joining branch setting
bounded_name_observations.scope: The map places Las Arenosas east of the selected northward lowland axis on a joining drainage. It does not name the entire selected northward continuation.

bounded_name_observations.name: El Milagro
bounded_name_observations.scope: A separate named waterbody east of the selected southern-to-middle corridor. Proximity to the chosen upper setting does not establish that the selected opening or whole composite is named El Milagro.

terminal_review.source_terminal: The stored source endpoint lies in the interior of the northern light-colored closed playa reached by the selected final alluvial approach.
terminal_review.render_terminal: The render endpoint coincides with the source endpoint in that same playa interior; it is not a separate downstream extension.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
